findings.description: The command 'show code --refresh-on-miss' passes the initial argument-count check. Removing the flag leaves only 'code', but the parser does not validate again. It passes an empty query to show(), which ordinarily produces a miss and can launch a foreground refresh when the graph is stale. The command then returns exit code 0 despite the missing required query. The mirrored adapter has the same behavior.
findings.evidence: Static inspection of main(), show(), and _show_code(). Existing GraphOnMiss tests cover valid queries but omit this malformed invocation.
findings.recommendation: Validate that a nonempty query remains after removing options; return usage error 2 before calling show().
findings.title: Removing the flag can leave an empty query and trigger a refresh
